text: For instance, MAS can impose stricter controls and processes to protect data from unauthorised use, in addition to the Personal Data Protection Act.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Mr Derrick Goh suggested a ratings system for payment service providers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But unlike the food and property development industries, payment service providers are licensed and subject to on-going supervision by MAS.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I would thus encourage consumers to ensure that the payment service providers they engage, such as the platform they use to buy or sell DPTs, are licensed by MAS.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Mr Saktiandi also asked if cyberattacks lead to massive losses, how will customers be compensated and what are the penalties.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In such an event, MAS will oversee the payment service provider’s dispute resolution process to ensure that they handle customer claims fairly and promptly.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The next set of risks raised by Members – Ms Ng Ling Ling, Mr Louis Ng, Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Saktiandi – pertain to fraud and scams.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The first set of actions to prevent this is to have a rigorous, robust, regulatory regime.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: MAS grants licences only to entities that have in place proper governance and risk management processes.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Further, MAS and the Commercial Affairs Department or CAD will take enforcement actions against entities that operate illegally or fail to comply with regulatory requirements.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In response to Mr Yip Hon Weng’s specific questions, our enforcement agencies have the power to investigate, seize and confiscate assets in their pursuit of DPT-related scam and fraud cases.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For example, two persons were convicted in 2020 for promoting an illegal pyramid scheme involving a purported fraudulent digital token called "OneCoin".

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Members are concerned that today’s enhancements could give consumers a false sense of security and encourage them to jump into DPT-related investments.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Some Members may recall we had this same debate, when we first tabled the Payment Services Bill in this House in January 2019, except the tables were then turned.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Then, there were requests that MAS regulate DPTs more strictly.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I explained that we were not ready to do so, because DPTs were still at a nascent stage of development and we should be mindful that more regulation may have a legitimising effect.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Compared to January 2019, while the usage of DPTs in Singapore remains low today, recent developments, such as stablecoins, can spur greater adoption of DPTs within a short time.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, it is timely to have new powers to be able to tighten the regulation, notwithstanding the concern of a legitimising effect.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The fact is DPTs remain unsuitable for most retail investors.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Placing funds in DPTs like bitcoins comes with very high risk.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They should seek to understand the product, its characteristics and risks before committing their money.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling is especially concerned about seniors and rightfully so.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: She suggested risk disclosures and suitability assessments for seniors.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked if there are measures to prevent false marketing to mislead customers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Financial advice received in relation to DPTs may be separately regulated under the Financial Advisers Act.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: However, potential investors should be aware that not all advice they receive in relation to DPT investments is regulated by MAS.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Only advice concerning investment products are regulated under the Financial Advisers Act.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Investors should check with their financial institutions if the particular DPT investment they are considering is a regulated investment product and understand the risks of dealing in unregulated investment products.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Where the digital tokens are used by issuers as a way to raise capital from the public, the issuers will be subject to the full set of regulatory requirements applicable for securities issuance —

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Excuse me, Minister Ong, if I may ask you to give way to Leader for the purposes of Exempted Business.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They voiced the concern of small players and licence holders being caught under the consumer protection requirements.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But this is where we also need to strike a balance.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We want to encourage entrepreneurship but, at the same time, need to protect consumers especially given the current circumstances that DPTs can become more popular, companies can come up with products that are more attractive.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And, today, what we are doing, we believe, is an appropriate and calibrated response.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As suggested by several Members, MAS will continue to educate the public on DPTs, through the national financial education programme, MoneySense.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will also explore ways to better reach out to seniors, such as through mainstream media channels, working with agencies such as IMDA and SkillsFuture Singapore, and through the communities.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MAS and the CAD have also rolled out consumer education initiatives to raise public awareness of the risks of putting their money in DPTs.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Since 2017, several advisories have been issued to warn the public of the risks and of common tactics used by scammers, to cheat people of their money or make use of them to carry out money laundering activities.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will continue our efforts, together with the industry and the community.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: He said that digital payment uptake is not fast enough.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But, actually, digital payment uptake in Singapore is quite rapid.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We can see many merchants taking up, individuals using, and this is after years of work putting in place infrastructure such as the FAST and PayNow system, which makes things a lot more convenient.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And then, the Singapore Quick Response Code (SGQR), a unified point-of-sale system.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, all these helped create a very strong momentum of digital payment uptake.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But when it comes to hawkers in coffeeshops, they are actually one of the hardest to convert.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But we will continue to work on them.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There are improvements that we can make including on the software, on the user interface as well as the user experience.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is something that MAS will continue to work with agencies, such as IMDA, to continue to push the process.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As DPTs have little or no intrinsic value, and their market value is highly volatile, they have not taken off in a big way as an accepted payment mode in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And it is actually quite a sensible outcome.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Don Wee asked for an assurance that DPTs should not be used as collateral to grant working capital loans.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Businesses and lenders must understand the nature of DPTs, and those that wish to accept DPTs either as payments or collateral for lending to DPT owners would thus have to bear the risk of value depreciation.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MAS conducts thematic checks on banks’ collateral management practices to ensure that they maintain prudent credit risk management.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There are, in fact, many alternatives to facilitate the normal conduct of business.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Saktiandi suggested a scheme similar to deposit insurance, to safeguard customers against potential losses.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Don Wee asked whether capital adequacy ratios would be imposed on DPT service providers.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Banks take in deposits and on-lend these funds.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They play a critical intermediating role in the economy and are, therefore, subject to stringent prudential regulation and supervision, including deposit insurance and capital adequacy ratios.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: DPT service providers are not banks, do not perform similar economic functions or pose similar systemic risks.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Such safeguards currently do not apply to DPT service providers.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To ensure all our regulations are not so onerous that we stifle entrepreneurship, let me reiterate the basic architecture of the Payment Services Act, which is that it is risk-based, three different licences, three different tiers, with requirements calibrated to the risk they pose, and taking a modular approach.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I want to assure him that the intent of the Act is to regulate entities that are carrying out payment services as a business and not for individuals.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I also want to assure Assoc Prof Jamus Lim that DPT service provided in respect of a central bank DPT function is also carved out in the Act currently.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The new user protection powers introduced under section 21A of the Act is to empower MAS to impose user protection requirements when needed.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It will not be implemented immediately, as I have explained.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The adoption of DPTs remains small in Singapore and it remains that we are regulating for ML/TF.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If MAS was to exercise the powers, the industry can be assured that we will keep to the principle of the Payment Services Act – risk-based, modular.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As such, it is likely that requirements will be imposed for major payment institutions first and if we do not detect the same concern for standard payment institutions.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim also asked about moneychangers and he highlighted that business is affected, and indeed so.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But it is really not due to this legislation.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Because of COVID-19, tourism has been affected badly, that has affected moneychangers' business quite adversely as well.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, new applicants that are seeking to enter the market will not enjoy this six months' grace period, which I think is reasonable.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As for higher limit on the stock and flow cap of e-money, as raised by Mr Louis Chua, we will continue to study the issue.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These caps are actually enshrined in the main Act, so if there are any changes to remove the caps, we will have to consult and come back to the House to make the necessary changes.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: On Mr Leon Perera and Mr Louis Chua's request for a success rate of application for DPT service provider licences, it is too early to provide a representative success rate currently.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Many require very close consultations, even hand-holding and guidance due to their unfamiliarity with AML requirements and the applicability of the Payment Services Act to their business.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, everyone is learning in this very fast moving and evolving space and MAS will continue to review how best to speed up the process and strike a good balance between encouraging entrepreneurship and regulation.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MAS seeks to ensure that its regulatory regime is aligned with international standards and that it has the necessary tools to respond quickly to market developments.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: With that Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, I beg to move.
